# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤟 ✌ ✌ 🤟 👍]

I need to relay what I see to Blind (who can hear me) and to Mute (via gesture, since Mute can see but not hear). Let me first note the gesture Mute sent me - I can see gestures but I don't yet have a shared code with Mute for what these symbols mean, so I can't interpret it meaningfully yet. I'll wait for more context but should start by giving Blind and Mute the raw bomb facts since that's the safest first move - Blind needs to know what's on the bomb, and Mute needs to know too since Mute has the manual and needs to match instructions to what's visible.

I'll speak (heard by Mute and Blind) describing the board plainly, and also gesture the same info to Mute in case Mute needs it visually too (though speak already reaches Mute). Actually speak reaches Mute and Blind both. That's efficient - one speak covers both listeners.

```
speak(text="Display shows 0. Light is yellow. There is a large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires: wire 1 blue, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👍 👎]

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👉", "👍"])
speak(text="Board unchanged: display 0, light yellow, button large labeled push to defuse, wires blue yellow red in order 1 2 3. Mute, I see your gestures but have no shared meaning yet.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Mute is now sending a single gesture ☝, likely trying to point to something specific — perhaps referencing wire 1, or asking me to focus on one detail. Without a prior agreed code, I can't be certain, but ☝ could conventionally mean "one" or "first". This might be Mute's attempt to ask "which wire is first / what is wire 1's color" or confirming something about item #1.

I should keep feeding Blind (who acts) the full picture via speech, and try to establish a simple gesture protocol with Mute since Mute can't hear or speak but can see my gestures. I'll propose using numbers via finger-count gestures to refer to wire positions, and thumbs up/down for yes/no, so Mute can direct me.

```
speak(text="Still unchanged: display 0, light yellow, large button PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝]

Mute responded with 👍 ☝ - possibly confirming "yes, one" - agreeing that ☝ means "wire 1" or "item 1". This could be building a shared vocabulary. Let me try to establish more clearly: I'll use ☝✌🤟 for wire numbers 1,2,3, and try to ask Mute what the manual needs regarding wire 1, using yes/no confirmation gestures since Mute can't speak.

Actually, I should think about what's most useful: Mute has the manual and needs to know the bomb's state, then needs to tell Blind what to do. But Mute can't speak to Blind directly (mute cannot speak). Mute can only gesture, and gestures reach only Deaf (me), not Blind. So Mute must relay instructions to Blind through me somehow - but I can't hear Mute's meaning through gesture unless we build a code, and even then I'd need to translate to speech for Blind.

This is the key insight: Mute -> gestures -> me (Deaf) -> I interpret -> I speak to Blind. So I need to build a numeric/yes-no code with Mute to extract manual instructions, then relay in speech to Blind.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "🤝"])
speak(text="Bomb unchanged: display 0, light yellow, button large PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires 1 blue 2 yellow 3 red. Blind, please hold - still coordinating with Mute on manual details.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 ☝ 👎]

```
speak(text="Board unchanged: display 0, light yellow, button large PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires 1 blue 2 yellow 3 red. Mute, trying to confirm which wire - please respond with a number gesture then thumbs up or down.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "🤞"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]

Mute sent ☝ 👍 - this looks like a direct response to my proposal: ☝ = wire 1, 👍 = yes/confirm. This suggests Mute is confirming something about wire 1 - likely that the manual says to cut/act on wire 1, or that wire 1 matches a condition in the manual.

Let me build on this. I'll try to establish clearer semantics: ☝✌🤟 = wire numbers 1/2/3, 👍=yes/correct, 👎=no/incorrect. I already proposed this last turn (☝✌🤟🤞 meaning "number then thumb"). Mute's reply of ☝👍 fits perfectly: "wire 1, yes".

This could mean the manual instruction is about wire 1 - possibly "cut wire 1" or "wire 1 is safe" or asking me to confirm wire 1's color. Since I already told Mute wire 1 is blue, maybe Mute is confirming they understood: "wire 1, yes [got it]".

I should now ask about the button and light using similar coded gestures, and relay progress to Blind. Let me introduce codes for other elements too - but I only have this turn to gesture to Mute. Let me push forward: ask if the wire to cut is wire 1.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "🤞"])
speak(text="Bomb unchanged: display 0, light yellow, button large PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires 1 blue 2 yellow 3 red. Blind, standby, working out manual instructions with Mute.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍 👍]

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has repeatedly signaled wire 1 with confirmation gestures. Current best reading: the manual points to wire 1, which is blue. Do not act yet - wait for explicit confirmation next round.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "🤞"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👌]

Mute changed the second symbol from 👍 to 👌 this time - possibly signaling something different, like "wire 1 is correct/perfect" or a different confirmation than plain yes. This might just be Mute's way of emphasizing "exactly wire 1" or it could mean something entirely different that I'm misreading due to lack of true shared code.

I need to be very careful here - I've been assuming meanings without true confirmation. Let me try a cleaner protocol: ask Mute to gesture the wire color name isn't possible (no color gestures), but I can ask yes/no about specific colors by pointing at wire numbers and having Mute confirm.

Given repeated ☝ signals across many turns, I'm fairly confident Mute is trying to tell me/Blind that wire 1 (blue) is the one to cut. The 👌 could just be an "OK/perfect" affirmation rather than a new meaning. I should relay this to Blind now with appropriate caution, and continue confirming with Mute.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute continues to signal wire 1 consistently across multiple turns, including an OK gesture just now. Growing confidence the instruction is: cut wire 1, which is blue. Still no explicit stop/danger signal from Mute. Awaiting one more confirmation before you act.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "🤞"])
```
